The term serves as the TD target, and its difference from the current estimate, defines the TD error that drives parameter updates. A separate target network Q ¯ \bar{Q} provides the bootstrap values in the TD target and is synchronized with the main network every F F steps. This decoupling stabilizes training by reducing feedback loops between evolving predictions and targets. To avoid unnecessary evaluations during stagnation, the framework employs an adaptive early termination criterion. If neither objective exhibits progress beyond tolerance thresholds ( ϵ r , ϵ e ) (\epsilon_{r},\epsilon_{e}) for T s T_{s} consecutive steps, the optimization loop is terminated. This stopping rule detects convergence to regions of marginal improvement and prevents excessive computation in performance plateaus, enhancing the overall efficiency of the EARL search process.
